Surf 2.20.0 adds an optional way to find and interact with page elements by describing what you need. You can combine those actions into short workflows and adjust confidence thresholds for individual commands without changing the safer defaults. On dynamic pages, Surf is more careful about checking whether a change worked before it proceeds. Windows Chrome setup from WSL is more reliable and easier to diagnose, alongside several everyday CLI fixes.

Surf 2.19.0 makes reliable page extraction available as a single command. Page automation can now distinguish ready, empty, login, challenge, missing, and error states instead of ending in an unclear timeout. New frame diagnostics make difficult iframe access problems easier to understand, while controlled inputs and script files behave more consistently in modern web apps. Remote users can also connect through TLS-terminating reverse proxies.

Surf 2.18.0 lets you record long browser sessions as local WebM videos and use GPT-6 Astra with Pro effort through Surf Oracle. ChatGPT automation now handles the current model menu and effort slider, checking your selections before sending a prompt. You can also clean up stale sessions or give a dedicated local user group access to Surf. Existing GIF recording and private-by-default socket access are unchanged.

Surf 2.17.0 makes GPT Pro Oracle runs more useful when you need ChatGPT to work with local context and repository-aware tools. You can now attach one local file to a new Oracle job or to a follow-up in the same conversation. You can also require ChatGPT's Chat mode with the GitHub tool before Surf submits the prompt, so repository-aware GPT Pro requests start in the right place. Text-only GPT Pro runs continue to work as before unless you opt into these new controls.

Surf 2.16.1 makes GPT Pro runs more dependable in reused ChatGPT tabs. Surf now clears leftover composer text before sending a prompt, so old manual test text no longer gets mixed into the next job. It also waits until the real prompt is present before checking Pro effort, which matches the current ChatGPT composer behavior. This is a small patch release focused on making text-only GPT Pro jobs and follow-ups feel stable again.

Surf 2.16.0 makes GPT Pro jobs smoother for Pi users. You can now build follow-up flows on top of Surf Oracle without losing track of the original conversation. Polling is less fragile because status checks can see completed GPT Pro jobs directly. Cancelled requests now stay cancelled, so interruption behavior is clearer and easier to trust.

Surf 2.15.1 makes the Pi GPT Pro path work as intended through Surf when ChatGPT is already open and logged in. It also makes device emulation less surprising by using the same aliases in the extension and native CLI paths. The docs now point users at the current release notes and the right help commands. This is a small patch release focused on reliability and clearer guidance.

Surf 2.15.0 makes multi-agent browser work practical. You can now give each agent its own named browser session that stays bound to one tab, and different sessions can run commands at the same time without stepping on each other. When something goes wrong, errors now include a copy-paste recovery command instead of leaving you to guess. Pi users also get an optional
agent that asks ChatGPT GPT-5.6 Sol Pro web mode directly through Surf.

shortcut now works with the current GPT-5.6 Sol picker, so agent workflows can keep using a stable alias while the visible ChatGPT label changes. This release should feel smoother if you depend on recoverable Oracle jobs or Pro-class ChatGPT dispatch.
